core_summary:
Chapter Overview & Pedagogical Purpose:
This chapter examines the defining scientific criteria that differentiate living organisms from non-living things. Sparked by Avadhi and Aayush's discovery of a live snail inside a quiet shell during a morning walk, students evaluate life processes: cellular movement, nutrition requirement, growth, respiration, response to stimuli (e.g., touch-me-not plant Chhui-mui), excretion, reproduction, and lifespan. It also examines seed germination as a transitional state showing latent life characteristics.
Full analysis of fundamental life characteristics, plant movement, environmental sensitivity, excretion, reproduction, and seed dormancy.

Detailed Section Breakdown & Curriculum Progression:
• 10.1 Defining Living vs Non-Living Entities:
  Living organisms exhibit all core life processes simultaneously: nutrition, growth, respiration, excretion, movement, response to stimuli, reproduction, and finite lifespan. Non-living objects may show one isolated trait (like a moving car) but lack metabolic life processes.
  Margin Insights: [Did You Know?: Living Snail Shells - A snail's hard protective shell is part of its living body and grows continuously along with the snail.]
• 10.2 Core Biological Characteristics of Life:
  1. Food / Nutrition: Energy source for cellular work and growth.
2. Growth: Irreversible increase in size and cell number.
3. Respiration: Biochemical oxidation of food to release cellular energy.
4. Response to Stimuli: Reaction to environmental changes (light, touch, temperature).
5. Excretion: Removal of toxic metabolic waste products.
6. Reproduction: Producing offspring of one's own kind.
7. Lifespan: Finite cycle of birth, growth, aging, and death.
• 10.3 Plant Movements and Sensitivity:
  Plants do not move from place to place (no locomotion) but show internal movement and tropisms. The Chhui-mui (Touch-me-not / Mimosa pudica) folds its leaves rapidly upon physical contact.
• 10.4 Latent Life in Dry Seeds:
  Dry seeds stored in sacks undergo minimal metabolic activity (dormancy or latent life). When provided with water, oxygen, and suitable temperature, seeds germinate into active seedlings.

Key Curricular Topics Covered:
• 10.1 Living vs. Non-Living - Classroom observation with pencil vs. pigeon.
• 10.2 Fundamental Characteristics of Life - Movement, food, growth, respiration, response to stimuli, excretion, reproduction.
• 10.3 Plant Movements & Sensitivity - Chhui-mui (Touch-me-not) response.
• 10.4 Latent Life in Seeds - Seed germination stages.

Key Practical Activities & Investigative Guidelines:
• Activity  (): Objective: . Procedure: Gently touch the tip of a leaflet on a fully expanded Chhui-mui leaf with a finger. -> Observe the rapid response of the leaflets and leaf stalk.. Key Observation: . Conclusion: Plants possess sensitivity and respond actively to external environmental stimuli..

key_concepts: Universal Life Processes (10.1 Living vs. Non-Living Criteria): Living organisms exhibit all core life processes simultaneously. Non-living objects may show an isolated feature (e.g., moving car, growing cloud) but lack internal metabolic cellular life processes. (Real-World Example/Activity: Comparing pigeon/snail (living) with pencil/car (non-living) in Table 10.1) [Key Terms: Living Entity, Non-Living Object, Life Processes]

Metabolism, Growth, and Reproduction (10.2 Fundamental Life Characteristics): Nutrition: Food provides energy for cellular maintenance and work. Growth: Irreversible internal increase in body size and cell count. Respiration: Biochemical breakdown of food in cells to release energy. Response to Stimuli: Functional reaction to external changes (light, touch, temperature). Excretion: Elimination of toxic metabolic waste products. Reproduction: Producing new individual offspring of one's own species. Lifespan: Finite cycle of birth, growth, maturation, aging, and death. (Real-World Example/Activity: Human breathing; animals eating food; plants growing towards sunlight) [Key Terms: Nutrition, Growth, Respiration, Stimuli, Excretion, Reproduction, Lifespan]

Sensitivity in Plants and Dormancy (10.3 Plant Movements and Seed Dormancy): Chhui-mui (Touch-me-not / Mimosa pudica): Demonstrates rapid leaf folding and drooping when touched. Latent Life in Seeds: Dry seeds in storage remain dormant with low metabolic rate; when supplied with water, air (oxygen), and warmth, they germinate into seedlings. (Real-World Example/Activity: Touching Chhui-mui leaves; germinating dry bean seeds on moist cotton) [Key Terms: Chhui-mui, Mimosa pudica, Stimulus Response, Seed Germination, Dormancy / Latent Life]
Universal Life Traits: All living things need food, respire, grow internally, respond to stimuli, excrete waste, reproduce, and have a defined lifespan.
Living vs Non-Living: Non-living objects (like cars or clouds) may show isolated movement or external growth but lack metabolic life processes.
Plant Sensitivity: Movement in response to touch stimulus (e.g., rapid leaf folding in Chhui-mui / Mimosa pudica).

key_terms.definition: The essential biological process by which living cells break down absorbed food molecules to release usable energy. (e.g., Inhaling oxygen to break down glucose into CO₂, water, and energy.)
The reaction of an organism to changes in its external environment. (e.g., Leaves of the Chhui-mui (Mimosa pudica) folding inward upon being touched.)
The removal of toxic metabolic waste products from an organism's body. (e.g., Exhaling carbon dioxide, sweating, urine elimination.)
Any change in an organism's external or internal environment that evokes a functional response. (e.g., Touch, light, heat, gravity, sound.)
A state of minimal metabolic activity in dry seeds that persists until favorable environmental conditions initiate germination.

key_takeaways: Living organisms perform multiple metabolic processes simultaneously to maintain life.
Respiration occurs continuously in all living cells, including plants and dormant seeds.
Plants respond actively to environmental stimuli such as light, gravity, and touch.
Curriculum Synthesis: Full analysis of fundamental life characteristics, plant movement, environmental sensitivity, excretion, reproduction, and seed dormancy.
Practical Takeaway (): Plants possess sensitivity and respond actively to external environmental stimuli.
